items.title: Assert Test
items.text:
Assert Test was created to test scenes using Godot built-in assert.

Warning

It's not a replacement for full-featured unit testing addons like GdUnit or Gut!

items.title: Memory Leak
items.text:
Is a classic problem that people normally don't notice until closing the game, because it's only then that Godot shows in the terminal a message like: 

WARNING: 1 ObjectDB instance was leaked at exit (run with `--verbose` for details).
    at: cleanup (core/object/object.cpp:2536)

Godot has three objects that interact with memory in a different way:

  • Object
  • Node
  • RefCounted

items.title: Object
items.text:
The classic "you allocated, you free it".

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Object.new()

    get_tree().quit()

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Object.new()

    a.free()

    get_tree().quit()

items.title: Cautions
items.text:
If your object is built from others objects, you need to remember to free every single one.

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends Object:
    var b := Object.new()

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()

    a.b.free()
    a.free()

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends Object:
    var b := Object.new()

items.title: Node
items.text:
When you free it, it will free the descedants before itself.

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Node.new()
    var b := Node.new()

    a.add_child(b)

    get_tree().quit()

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Node.new()
    var b := Node.new()

    a.add_child(b)
    a.free()

    get_tree().quit()

items.title: Cautions
items.text:
If you remove a Node from it parent, you have to remember to manually free it later.

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Node.new()
    var b := Node.new()

    a.add_child(b)
    a.remove_child(b)

    get_tree().quit()

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Node.new()
    var b := Node.new()

    a.add_child(b)
    a.remove_child(b)
    a.free()
    b.free()

    get_tree().quit()

Do not confuse children with properties, a Node in the property needs to freed manually.

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()

    a.free()

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends Node:
    var b := Node.new()

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()

    a.b.free()
    a.free()

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends Node:
    var b := Node.new()

items.title: RefCounted
items.text:
It will free itself when no one reference it anymore. 

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := RefCounted.new()

    get_tree().quit()

items.title: Cautions
items.text:
Avoid circular reference, otherwise it will never free itself.

Memory leakFix 
func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()
    var b := Example.new()

    a.r = b
    b.r = a

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends RefCounted:
    var r: RefCounted = null

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()
    var b := Example.new()

    a.r = weakref(b)
    b.r = weakref(a)

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends RefCounted:
    var r: WeakRef = null

WeakRef will not increase the reference count and to get back the reference use get_ref().

Losing the autocomplete

WeakRef.get_ref() returns a Variant, which means that you lose the autocomplete and needs to convert back to the correct type. One way that to solve this (instead of always converting) is to create an intermediary class like: 

func _ready() -> void:
    var a := Example.new()
    var b := Example.new()

    a.r = RefExample.new(b)
    b.r = RefExample.new(a)

    get_tree().quit()


class Example extends RefCounted:
    var r: RefExample = null


class RefExample extends RefCounted:
    var r: WeakRef = null

    func _init(e: Example) -> void:
        r = weakref(e)

    func get_ref() -> Example:
        return r.get_ref() as Example

items.title: Quitting
items.text:
A very important part of these tests is knowing how to quit(). So pay attention to these details:

  • quit(): Will quit the application at the end of current iteration
  • assert(): Failing will make the function return but the application continues running

items.title: Don't assert() before quit()
items.text:
The following code will never call the quit() because the assert() will fail and make the function return. 

func _ready() -> void:
    assert(false)

    # Never called.
    get_tree().quit()

But the next code will work because quit() continues with the function code: 

func _ready() -> void:
    get_tree().quit()

    # Called.
    assert(false)

Info

This is not unique of assert(), Godot handle unexpected erros by making the function return it default value.

items.title: Always set timeout
items.text:
An error can happen in any part of your code and the worst is happening before your quit(). For example: 

func _ready() -> void:
    var x = 10
    var y = Object.new()

    print(x + y)

    # Never called.
    get_tree().quit()

If this happens, you will only know when AssertScene timeout and by default this is 30 seconds, which is a lot... So I always recommend to reduce to an expected value.

items.title: Creating a test
items.text:
• Create a scene to be tested
  • Add as many assert() you wanto to validate if everything is working right
  • End the scene with get_tree().quit()

Note

Notice how we didn't use any feature from the addon to create the test.

  • Our scene doesn't have a Node from the addon
  • Our files doesn't need prefix/suffix test
  • Our methods doesn't need prefix/suffix test
  • Our script doesn't have to extend an addon script
  • Our script doesn't call method from the addon

The test is just a scene that close itself!

items.title: Running a test
items.text:
The first step is to create a scene which will be responsible for running your test scenes. It should have an AssertReport with one or more AssertScene as children.

Info

  • AssertReport initiate the children tests and print their results
  • AssertScene run the test scene in a new process

Access your AssertScene properties and put your test scene in the scene property.

Save this scene and execute it to start the tests! Your output should be something like:

No errorAssert failTimeoutedMemory leak 
(OK) Test description here
(1 OK, 0 FAIL)

(FAIL) Test description here
    SCRIPT ERROR: Assertion failed: assert message here
            ...

(0 OK, 1 FAIL)

(FAIL) Test description here --- Scene halted after exceeding time limit

(0 OK, 1 FAIL)

(FAIL) Test description here
    WARNING: 1 ObjectDB instance was leaked at exit (run with `--verbose` for details).
        at: cleanup (core/object/object.cpp:2536)

(0 OK, 1 FAIL)

It's basically the result of your test scene and the stderr messages.

items.title: Running multiple tests
items.text:
To run multiple tests, just add more AssertScene to your scene.

If you have many tests and wants to organize them, you can put AssertReport inside AssertReport.
